title: Distribution of Terms
short: A term is distributed when the proposition says something about every member of its class: A distributes S, E both, I neither, O the predicate.
trouble: Learners memorize the chart without the reason. "Some S are not P" excludes the S from all of P, so it speaks about every P.

blocks.html: Look again at the four forms. Some of them say something about every member of a class; others speak about only part of it. A term is distributed in a proposition when the proposition says something about every member of the class it names.

head: Form
Subject
Predicate
rows: O: Some S are not P
blocks.cap: Universals distribute the subject; negatives distribute the predicate.

blocks.html: Universal statements (A, E) distribute their subject. Negative statements (E, O) distribute their predicate. So A distributes S, E both, I neither, O only P.

Take each form in turn. "All S are P" speaks of every S, but only of the P that happen to be S. "No S are P" shuts every S out of the whole of P, which says of every P that it is not an S: both terms. "Some S are P" speaks of at least one S and at least one P: neither class as a whole. "Some S are not P" speaks of only some S, but says that whole class P leaves those S out, so it tells us something about every P: the predicate.

blocks.name: lg-syllogism
blocks.cap: In an O proposition only the predicate term is distributed (underlined).

blocks.title: An A proposition
blocks.q: Which terms are distributed in "All dancers are musicians"?
steps: It is universal, so the subject dancers is distributed: it speaks of every dancer.
It is affirmative, so the predicate musicians is not: it does not speak of every musician.

blocks.title: An O proposition
blocks.q: Which terms are distributed in "Some readers are not bakers"?
steps: It is particular, so readers is not distributed.
It is negative, so bakers is distributed: every baker is outside the group of readers it mentions.

blocks.name: lg-syllogism
blocks.cap: Your turn: tap every distributed term, then Check.

blocks.html: Memorizing the chart without the reason, then forgetting the O form. "Some S are not P" excludes some S from all of P, so it speaks about every P. Check by asking, for each term, "Does this statement say something about every one of these?"

sources.name: Patrick J. Hurley, A Concise Introduction to Logic, 4.2 Quality, Quantity, and Distribution
